channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound: Political risks and BoE stance shape outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses British Pound (GBP) prospects around UK welfare reform, shifting voter polls and the upcoming Bank of England (BoE) decision. Foley highlights how PM Burnham’s fiscal choices and intra-Labour tensions could affect gilts and the Pound.

item.title: Trump downplays escalation risks while warning Iran against breaking agreements
item.description: In an interview with Fox News, cited by Reuters, US President Donald Trump said that Pickaxe Mountain, an Iranian underground nuclear site, is not a big problem, adding that the United States (US) is now in a very strong position with Iran.

item.title: Copper: Tight supply underpins constructive outlook – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Copper has extended its July gains as easing Middle East tensions lift sentiment. They point to tight physical conditions, low inventories and firm Chinese import demand as key supports.

item.title: $4,000: Gold’s key support faces a crucial Fed test
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Tuesday, pressured by a firmer US Dollar (USD), even as Oil prices extend their pullback on hopes of an end to the US-Iran war. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,034, down 1.0% on the day, after failing to sustain gains above $4,100 on Monday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Scenarios into FOMC – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Eugene Leow notes that investors remain cautious on upcoming FOMC decisions, with markets pricing a 34% chance of a July hike and nearly full odds for September.

item.title: Euro nears three-week high against British Pound on UK fiscal concerns, BoE outlook
item.description: EUR/GBP holds firm on Tuesday, extending its recovery from the more than one-year low touched earlier this month as diverging monetary policy expectations between the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Bank of England (BoE), along with UK fiscal concerns, weigh on the British Pound (GBP).

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles as firm US Dollar keeps NZD/USD pinned
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5770 on Tuesday at the time of writing, slightly lower on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains pressured by the firm US Dollar (USD), which continues to benefit from safe-haven demand amid persistent geopolitical tensions.

item.title: US ADP Employment Change 4-week average drops to 15K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has further cooled in mid-July. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 15K jobs per week in the four weeks ending July 11.

item.title: Analysts warn: The market might be ahead of itself with the recent Oil sell-off
item.description: Crude Oil prices hold at one-week lows on Tuesday, after having depreciated more than 12% from last week's highs.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Tariffs and steady SNB stance pressure currency – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister notes that reports of the Swiss National Bank (SNB) planning to keep rates unchanged until early 2028, if accurate, clash with still-ambitious market expectations for hikes by 2027.

item.title: British Pound drops against US Dollar, Fed-BoE policy in focus
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends its decline against the US Dollar (USD) to near 1.3277 during the European trading session on Tuesday, the lowest level seen in over three weeks.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Inflation risks keep hike debate alive – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) preferred core Consumer Price Index (CPI) to rise 0.9% q/q in Q2, matching consensus and up from 0.8% in Q1. This would lift annual core inflation to 3.7%, just below the RBA’s 3.8% projection.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Under pressure with YTD lows at 1.1324 coming closer
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is failing to draw any significant support from the truce in the Middle East and the lower Oil prices and keeps heading south against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. EUR/USD bears are testing fresh one-month lows below 1.1360, drawing near the year-to-date low of 1.1324.

item.title: CEE FX: Normalising rates leave room for gains – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes Central and Eastern European (CEE) rate curves have repriced sharply, with more tightening now expected in Czech Republic and Poland and further easing in Hungary.

item.title: Indian Rupee reflects strength amid lower oil prices, Fed policy eyed
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends its winning streak against the US Dollar (USD) for the third trading day on Tuesday. The USD/INR pair falls to near 95.65 as a further decline in oil prices has strengthened the Indian currency.

item.title: Australian Dollar underperforms after RBA Bullock’s remarks on economy
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is down against its major currency peers, trading 0.35% lower at around 0.6965 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen stays range-bound as Fed, BoJ seen on hold but hawkish
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 163.90 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.11% on the day, as investors remain cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy decision on Wednesday and the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) policy announcement on Friday.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Leadership change at BI sustains rupiah pressure – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Moses Lim argues that Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo’s surprise resignation, following earlier high-profile departures, heightens concerns over policy continuity and institutional credibility as the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) trades near historic lows versus the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $57.53 per troy ounce, down 1.49% from the $58.40 it cost on Monday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed hike odds and asymmetric risks – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee notes that the Dollar is trading on diverging themes versus Developed Market and Asia-ex Japan currencies, with Fed expectations central. Futures are pricing a 38% chance of a surprise rate hike at Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s second FOMC meeting.

item.title: Silver weakens as easing geopolitical tensions weigh on safe-haven demand
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $57.55 on Tuesday at the time of writing, down 1.45% on the day, as investors remain cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's (Fed) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS surprise tightening supports SGD – HSBC
item.description: HSBC’s Abhilash Narayan notes that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy on 27 July 2026 by raising the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope to 1.25%.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Lower oil prices ensure further weakness for Canadian Dollar
item.description: The USD/CAD pair trades marginally lower to near 1.4113 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The Loonie pair edges down as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) outperforms its major currency peers.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Risk-off and RBA tone weigh on Aussie – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman reports the Australian Dollar (AUD) has been the worst performing G10 currency overnight despite being the best performer year-to-date.

item.title: Swiss Franc: SNB on hold view boosts funding role – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights a Bloomberg source story suggesting the Swiss National Bank (SNB) may keep its policy rate at 0.00% until end-2027, aligning with ING’s own forecast.

item.title: Gold languishes below $4,050; eyes further losses as focus remains on FOMC decision
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its offered tone through the first half of the European session on Tuesday and currently trades just below $4,050, down nearly 0.80% for the day.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Close July call keeps Dollar traders data-focused – BNY
item.description: BNY strategists John Velis and David Tam expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at the upcoming July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, while stressing it is a close call.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Political fragmentation clouds zloty outlook – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose highlights that Poland’s Law and Justice party has split, with Mateusz Morawiecki forming Development Plus and polling above the Sejm threshold.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar shows resilience ahead of Fed meeting
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, July 28:

item.title: US Dollar: Stronger into FOMC on hawkish expectations – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar (USD) has reversed early-week losses and is trading near year-to-date highs ahead of tomorrow’s Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
